subject: Logic
title: Testing Validity with Tables
description: Learn Testing Validity with Tables in one minute.

hook.text: Is this argument valid? Build a truth table and the answer jumps out—no guesswork required.

buildup.text: An argument is valid if every row where all premises are true also makes the conclusion true.

discovery.text: Find the rows where premises are true. If even one has a false conclusion, the argument is invalid.

twist.text: A valid argument can have false premises. Validity only guarantees: true inputs → true output.

climax.text: Truth tables give a mechanical, objective test. No intuition needed—just follow the rows.

quiz.question: How do truth tables test validity?
options: Check if the conclusion is always true
Check that true premises always yield a true conclusion
